title: Russia's diesel export ban: the middle-distillate value chain
map_limitation: Three blind spots specific to THIS map. (1) The root is unbuyable and undisclosed: Rosneft, Lukoil, Gazprom Neft and Surgutneftegas are sanctioned and file nothing this venue can read, so russian-refining-attrition carries zero tickers by design and every volume on it is a third-party estimate (KSE Institute, Insights Global, Platts assessments quoted in trade press), never an issuer disclosure. (2) Supplier-side EDGAR full-text search cannot see this chain's gating suppliers. Topsoe, Axens, Grace / Advanced Refining Technologies, Oiltanking, VTTI, Insights Global and Dangote Industries are private, and the listed names that matter file outside the SEC: BAS.DE, CLN.SW, JMAT.L, AI.PA, 4091.T, 5631.T, 034020.KS, LT.NS, 009540.KS, 010140.KS, 042660.KS, 600150.SS, BS6.SI, NESTE.HE, MOH.AT, REP.MC, RELIANCE.NS, IOC.NS, 010950.KS, TOP.BK, 600028.SS, 2222.SR, DIS.MI, 9104.T, VPK.AS, RUI.PA, SNI.OL, ODF.OL, DCC.L, 8133.T, BHP.AX, MAERSK-B.CO, CVE.TO, SU.TO, EQNR.OL, 0857.HK, 0386.HK, SHEL.L and GBF.DE. Those reach the map through research, not through fts, which is the inherited v8 limitation biting hardest at the two links the thesis depends on. (3) Two quantities the thesis rests on are directionally sourced and quantitatively soft: nobody cited here publishes ULSD-capable hydrocracking capacity by owner, so conversion-capacity is ordered by narrative complexity rather than by a disclosed unit list; and the LR2 rate series is a Platts index quoted in secondary press rather than fetched, so it is INFERRED and cannot be re-derived. The map also cannot see the shadow-fleet tonnage idled from the old Baltic short-haul trade, which is latent clean-tanker capacity with no public register and is this chain's most likely quiet invalidation.

links.name: Crude feedstock and the heavy sour barrel
links.role: The raw input the whole chain converts: complex refiners buy discounted heavy, high-sulfur crude, and it is the heavy end of that barrel, not light sweet crude, that a conversion unit turns into middle distillate.

evidence.claim: Sour coking margins measured against WCS expanded to around $20/bbl, compared with roughly $15/bbl during the same period a year earlier, while US refinery capacity utilisation stood close to 90%, roughly 5 pp above typical seasonal averages, and heavy sour grades remained under pressure relative to light sweet benchmarks.
evidence.source_name: Kpler, US Refinery Utilisation Near Multi-Year Seasonal Highs
source_excerpt: Sour coking margins (vs WCS) have expanded to around $20/bbl in Q1-26 (QTD), compared with roughly $15/bbl during the same period last year
US refinery capacity utilisation stood close to 90%, roughly 5 pp above typical seasonal averages
Following geopolitical shifts and the return of Venezuelan crude into the open market, heavy sour grades have remained under pressure relative to light sweet benchmarks.

evidence.claim: Hydrocracking is increasingly the preferred pathway to upgrade residues and vacuum gasoils into valuable middle distillates, so the heavy end of the crude barrel is the physical feed a conversion unit consumes.
evidence.source_name: PR Times, Hydrocracker Market Set to Expand at a 5.5% CAGR Through 2032 Amid Rising Diesel Demand
source_excerpt: hydrocracking is increasingly the preferred pathway to upgrade residues and vacuum gasoils into valuable middle distillates and petrochemical feedstocks

bottleneck.note: Crude is abundant and fungible and the market already priced this layer. The shortage on this map is a conversion problem, not a feedstock problem.

capture_inputs.substitutability: High. Grades are interchangeable within a configuration and the discount, not the availability, is what moves.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not the producer on this occurrence: the cited margin expansion accrues to the coking and conversion refiner buying the discounted barrel, not to the seller of it.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: 2222.SR also appears on refinery-capacity-response; the same issuer is both feedstock seller and capacity adder, so it is one bet wearing two link labels.

links.name: Hydroprocessing catalyst
links.role: Hydrotreating and hydrocracking catalyst is the consumable that decides how much on-spec ultra-low-sulfur diesel a given unit yields per pass, and it is reloaded on a cycle rather than bought once.

evidence.claim: Catalyst suppliers differentiate on cycle life, selectivity toward distillates or naphtha, and the ability to handle heavier feeds, and these attributes materially affect unit margins and maintenance cadence; the companies profiled in depth are Honeywell UOP, Axens, Shell Catalysts & Technologies, Chevron Lummus Global, Topsoe, Albemarle, BASF SE, ExxonMobil, Sinopec Catalyst Co. and Johnson Matthey.
evidence.source_name: PR Times, Hydrocracker Market Set to Expand at a 5.5% CAGR Through 2032 Amid Rising Diesel Demand
source_excerpt: Catalyst suppliers differentiate on cycle life, selectivity toward distillates or naphtha, and the ability to handle heavier feeds; these attributes materially affect unit margins and maintenance cadence.

Key companies we profile in-depth include Honeywell UOP, Axens, Shell Catalysts & Technologies, Chevron Lummus Global (CLG), Topsoe, Albemarle, BASF SE, ExxonMobil, Sinopec Catalyst Co., and Johnson Matthey.

evidence.claim: Regulatory tightening on sulfur and emissions is sustaining demand for ultra-low-sulfur diesel and jet fuel, which is the demand the catalyst charge inside a conversion unit exists to serve.
evidence.source_name: PR Times, Hydrocracker Market Set to Expand at a 5.5% CAGR Through 2032 Amid Rising Diesel Demand
source_excerpt: Regulatory tightening on sulfur and emissions...is sustaining demand for ultra-low-sulfur diesel and jet fuel
hydrocracking is increasingly the preferred pathway to upgrade residues and vacuum gasoils into valuable middle distillates and petrochemical feedstocks

bottleneck.note: A short, licensor-affiliated supplier list, several members private (Topsoe, Axens, Grace), and each charge is qualified to a specific unit, so it is not a spot purchase.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: The cited profile names ten suppliers for the whole hydroprocessing catalyst and licensing space, three of the most technically relevant of which (Topsoe, Axens, Grace) are not listed.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Low within a cycle: a catalyst system is qualified per unit and changed at turnaround, so a refiner cannot switch supplier when the crack moves.
capture_inputs.logistics_or_qualification: Qualification, not logistics. The barrier is the unit-specific performance guarantee, which is also why the sale travels with the licence.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: NULL at map time. No catalyst-segment margin for this episode is cited here; the refiner margin is the one on the record.

links.name: Refinery hydrogen supply
links.role: Every atom of sulfur removed and every heavy molecule cracked consumes hydrogen, which reaches the refinery from an on-site or over-the-fence plant owned by an industrial gas company under a long-term contract.

evidence.claim: A 25 million-standard-cubic-foot-per-day unit was built next to the Delaware City Refinery, which it supplies with hydrogen to remove sulfur from crude products developed in other refining processes.
evidence.source_name: Industrial Info Resources, Linde plc's $2.2 Billion in Projects Fueled by Hydrogen, Petrochemical Needs
source_excerpt: The 25 million-standard-cubic-foot-per-day unit will be built next to the Delaware City Refinery, which it will supply with hydrogen to remove sulfur from crude products developed in other refining processes.

evidence.claim: Air Liquide secured new long-term hydrogen supply agreements that significantly reinforce its presence in Texas and is deploying nearly 50 million USD of targeted infrastructure upgrades tied to the hydrogen cavern it owns and operates at Spindletop, Texas.
evidence.source_name: Air Liquide, Air Liquide strengthens its U.S. Gulf Coast footprint and invests 50 million USD to support new long-term hydrogen supply agreements
source_excerpt: Air Liquide has secured new long-term hydrogen supply agreements that will significantly reinforce its presence in Texas
nearly 50 million USD
the world's largest hydrogen cavern in Spindletop, Texas

bottleneck.note: Hydrogen cannot be moved far economically, so each refinery gate is a local monopoly held on a long-dated contract. The constraint is logistics, not chemistry.

capture_inputs.substitutability: Low at the gate: an on-site or over-the-fence plant is a sunk asset next to one customer, and self-build is the only alternative.
capture_inputs.logistics_or_qualification: This is the ARCH-004 logistics leg in its purest form. Pipelines and caverns, not molecules, create the pricing power; the cited Gulf Coast position rests on an owned cavern and connected network.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: NULL at map time. The cited contracts are long-term take-or-pay in shape, which is the argument for durability, not a disclosed margin for this episode.

links.name: Hydrocracker licensing and heavy reactor hardware
links.role: New or revamped conversion capacity is licensed from a handful of process owners who also sell the catalyst and the reactor internals, and the thick-wall pressure vessels come from a short list of heavy fabrication shops.

evidence.claim: Chevron Lummus Global was awarded a licensing contract by Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited for an integrated hydrocracker and catalytic dewaxing unit at Mumbai Refinery in India with a nameplate capacity of 550 KTPA, on the strength of deep expertise in hydroprocessing technologies.
evidence.source_name: Lummus Technology, Chevron Lummus Global Awarded New Licensing Contract for HPCL's Integrated Hydrocracker and Catalytic Dewaxing Unit
source_excerpt: a nameplate capacity of 550 KTPA and will facilitate the production of Gr. II+ and Gr. III premium base oils
deep expertise in hydroprocessing technologies

evidence.claim: The same short list owns both the process and the catalyst: the companies profiled in depth are Honeywell UOP, Axens, Shell Catalysts & Technologies, Chevron Lummus Global, Topsoe, Albemarle, BASF SE, ExxonMobil, Sinopec Catalyst Co. and Johnson Matthey, and catalyst suppliers differentiate on cycle life and the ability to handle heavier feeds.
evidence.source_name: PR Times, Hydrocracker Market Set to Expand at a 5.5% CAGR Through 2032 Amid Rising Diesel Demand
source_excerpt: Key companies we profile in-depth include Honeywell UOP, Axens, Shell Catalysts & Technologies, Chevron Lummus Global (CLG), Topsoe, Albemarle, BASF SE, ExxonMobil, Sinopec Catalyst Co., and Johnson Matthey.

Catalyst suppliers differentiate on cycle life, selectivity toward distillates or naphtha, and the ability to handle heavier feeds; these attributes materially affect unit margins and maintenance cadence.

evidence.claim: The global hydrocracker market value reached approximately USD 75.7 billion in 2025 and the sector is anticipated to grow at 5.5% CAGR across 2026-2032, which is the spending line that any new conversion capacity has to pass through.
evidence.source_name: PR Times, Hydrocracker Market Set to Expand at a 5.5% CAGR Through 2032 Amid Rising Diesel Demand
source_excerpt: global hydrocracker market value...reached approximately USD 75.7 billion in 2025
5.5% CAGR across 2026–2032

bottleneck.note: ARCH-001 shape: licence availability and heavy-wall fabrication slots, not steel or money, set how fast conversion capacity can be added. Two of the four leading licensors (Axens, Topsoe) are private.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Four licensors carry most hydrocracking: Honeywell UOP, Axens, Shell Catalysts & Technologies and Chevron Lummus Global, per the cited profile. Two are not investable.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Low at project sanction, high before it: an owner picks a licensor once, then is locked to that catalyst and internals for the unit's life.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: HON and the catalyst link share one bill of materials. Owning HON for the licence and ALB for the catalyst is closer to one bet on hydroprocessing spend than to two.

links.name: Turnaround, catalyst handling and inspection services
links.role: A run-maximisation regime defers turnarounds and then forces them, so the specialist contractors who change catalyst beds, replace exchanger bundles and inspect desulfurization units carry the work the refiners postponed.

evidence.claim: Industrial Info Resources tracked $1.1 billion in U.S. refinery maintenance projects scheduled to begin in the opening quarter, with ExxonMobil, Marathon and Valero accounting for nearly half, while Citgo Lake Charles deferred a scheduled turnaround to sustain output during the strong margin environment.
evidence.source_name: BIC Magazine, What record refinery margins mean for Gulf Coast contractors
source_excerpt: Industrial Info Resources tracked $1.1 billion in U.S. refinery maintenance projects scheduled to begin in Q1 2026, with ExxonMobil, Marathon and Valero accounting for nearly half.
Citgo Lake Charles deferred a scheduled turnaround from Q4 2025 into 2026 to sustain output during the strong Q4 margin environment.

evidence.claim: Gulf Coast refinery utilization rates, which were running in the mid-80% range, pushed back toward maximum throughput almost immediately, and the scopes in demand are coker maintenance experience, heat exchanger bundle replacement capabilities or desulfurization unit expertise: the service input a refinery running flat out consumes.
evidence.source_name: BIC Magazine, What record refinery margins mean for Gulf Coast contractors
source_excerpt: Gulf Coast refinery utilization rates, which were running in the mid-80% range through most of 2025, pushed back toward maximum throughput almost immediately.
coker maintenance experience, heat exchanger bundle replacement capabilities or desulfurization unit expertise

bottleneck.note: ARCH-002 shape: competitively bid maintenance labour with high visible volume and a low capture ceiling, except where the scope is genuinely specialised (catalyst handling, high-pressure desulfurization units).

capture_inputs.substitutability: High for general mechanical scope, low for catalyst handling and high-pressure unit inspection, which is where the archetype's capture ceiling can be beaten.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: NULL at map time. The cited $1.1 billion is a work-value figure, not a contractor margin, and the trap this archetype exists to catch is reading one as the other.

links.name: Russian refining attrition and the export decree
links.role: The disruption itself and this map's uninvestable root: drone strikes have taken Russian refineries offline and a rolling decree keeps the remaining diesel and gasoil at home, so the volume that used to clear from the Baltic is simply not offered.

evidence.claim: Russia said on Saturday it had extended a ban on diesel exports until September 30, also covering exports of marine fuel and gas oils shipped by Russian producers, with several refineries still offline after repeated Ukrainian drone attacks; exports of diesel by non-producers and motor gasoline are banned until January 31, 2027 and jet fuel until the end of November 2026.
evidence.source_name: Asharq Al-Awsat, Russia Extends Ban on Diesel Exports Until September 30
source_excerpt: Russia said on Saturday it had extended a ban on diesel exports until September 30.
The ban also covers exports of marine fuel and gas oils shipped by Russian producers.
with several refineries still offline after repeated Ukrainian drone attacks.
Russia has also banned exports of diesel by non-producers and motor gasoline until January 31, 2027.
and jet fuel until the end of November 2026.

evidence.claim: Russia had previously exported a steady 900,000 to 1 million barrels of diesel and gasoil per day, whereas in June, following strikes on refineries, exports fell to approximately 580,000 barrels per day, and the ban is potentially putting up to 36% of its total oil product export volumes at risk while oil product exports fell by 13.1% to around 1.6 million barrels per day, the lowest level on record.
evidence.source_name: Kyiv School of Economics Institute, Russian Oil Tracker, July 2026
source_excerpt: Russia had previously exported a steady 900,000–1 million barrels of diesel and gasoil per day, whereas in June, following strikes on refineries, exports fell to approximately 580,000 barrels per day.
Russia banned diesel and gasoil exports in July 2026, potentially putting up to 36% of its total oil product export volumes at risk.
Oil product exports, by contrast, fell by 13.1% to around 1.6 million barrels per day—the lowest level on record.

evidence.claim: Russian crude processing fell to an average of 3.91 million barrels of crude per day in early July, more than 1.4 million barrels daily below the previous year's average, after Ukraine hit at least 24 of Russia's 34 large refineries in roughly 50 attacks over the past 100 days, and Turkey, Brazil, North Africa and Central Asia must now obtain barrels from the United States, India and the Middle East instead.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-003 inverted: this link sets every other link's demand and there is no instrument for it. Rosneft, Lukoil, Gazprom Neft and Surgutneftegas are sanctioned and unreachable from this venue, so the ticker list is deliberately empty.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Total for the volume at issue, and entirely outside the investable set. Every number on this link is a third-party estimate (KSE Institute), not an issuer disclosure.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Nobody on this link. The margin shows up two links downstream, at conversion-capacity and clean-product-shipping.

links.name: Product tanker newbuild slots
links.role: How fast the clean-tanker fleet can grow is set by yard slots rather than by owner appetite, and the yards are sold out years ahead, which is why a product-tanker rate spike does not self-correct on the usual cycle.

evidence.claim: The total global orderbook now stands at 191 million CGT, which represents 17 percent of the world's fleet, the highest such proportion since 2011; tankers accounted for 32 percent of total orders, Chinese shipyards secured 70 percent of all orders in the first quarter and South Korean yards captured 20 percent, and more than half of the orders placed this year are expected to be delivered after 2028.
evidence.source_name: IndexBox, Shipbuilding Orderbook at 17-Year Peak: 2026 Q1 Analysis & Trends
source_excerpt: The total global orderbook now stands at 191 million CGT, which represents 17 percent of the world's fleet, the highest such proportion since 2011.
Tankers accounted for 32 percent of total orders, their highest share since mid-2017.

Chinese shipyards maintained a dominant position, securing 70 percent of all orders in the first quarter of 2026. South Korean yards captured 20 percent, a share largely supported by stronger LNG tanker ordering.
More than half of the orders placed this year expected to be delivered after 2028.

evidence.claim: The constraint is physical, with every dock occupied and every slot spoken for, and an order signed in mid-2026 will, for most major yards, produce a ship in 2029 or 2030, so the fleet available to carry the rerouted barrel cannot grow on the timescale of the disruption.
evidence.source_name: Fairway ETA, The Yards Cannot Build Two Things at Once
source_excerpt: The constraint is physical.
Every dock occupied. Every slot spoken for.
An order signed in mid-2026 will, for most major yards, produce a ship in 2029 or 2030.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-001 shape on water: dock capacity, not order appetite, gates the fleet response, and the cited delivery dates put the response outside this occurrence's window.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Chinese yards took 70 percent of first-quarter orders and Korean yards 20 percent, per the cited orderbook, so two national yard complexes clear nine of every ten slots.
capture_inputs.substitutability: None inside the window: a slot is a slot, and the cited lead time is three to four years.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: NULL at map time. Yard order intake is cited; yard margin is not, and a full book at fixed-price contracts is the archetype's classic volume-without-capture risk.

links.name: ULSD-capable conversion capacity
links.role: This chain's actual scarcity: hydrocracking and deep desulfurization capacity, not crude, decides who can make on-spec ultra-low-sulfur diesel, and the units that have it are already running at the top of the utilization record.

evidence.claim: The diesel crack spread record high of $102.20 per barrel on August 17, 2026 marked the first occasion in history that refining margins for distillate fuel exceeded triple digits, against a typical range of roughly $20 to $40 per barrel, with U.S. diesel inventories entering late August at their lowest level since 1996.
evidence.source_name: Discovery Alert, Diesel Crack Spread Shatters Records With $102 High in 2026
source_excerpt: The diesel crack spread record high of $102.20 per barrel on August 17, 2026 marked the first occasion in history that refining margins for distillate fuel exceeded triple digits.
Under stable market conditions, diesel crack spreads typically trade in a range of roughly $20 to $40 per barrel.
U.S. diesel inventories entering late August 2026 stood at their lowest level since 1996, a 30-year trough that dramatically amplified the market's price response to each supply disruption.

evidence.claim: US refineries are running at 97.4% of operable capacity as of August 21, 2026, up 0.2 points week over week, a reading that sits near the high end of the EIA record going back to 1990, meaning the existing units have no headroom left to answer the shortage with.
evidence.source_name: The Vault Report, US Refinery Utilization
source_excerpt: US refineries are running at 97.4% of operable capacity as of August 21, 2026, up 0.2 points week over week.
Today's reading sits near the high end of the EIA record going back to 1990. High utilization means refineries are running hard, pulling crude from storage and adding finished product.

evidence.claim: European diesel refining margins rose above $60 per barrel following the export ban, and Turkey, Brazil, North Africa and Central Asia obtain barrels from the United States, India and the Middle East instead, which are the seaborne origins that replaced the short-haul supply.
evidence.source_name: OilPrice.com, As Ukraine Cripples Russian Refining, Global Diesel Markets Pay the Price
source_excerpt: European diesel refining margins rose above $60 per barrel
Those buyers now compete with countries already replacing delayed Gulf products

bottleneck.note: The ARCH-001 tell in this chain's own words: conversion capacity, not crude supply, has gated diesel output through this episode. Coverage is dense at the US large-cap end and much thinner across Europe, India and Southeast Asia.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: NULL at map time and this is the map's central gap: no source cited here publishes ULSD-capable hydrocracking capacity by owner, so the link is ranked by narrative complexity rather than by a disclosed unit list.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Low inside the window. Utilization at 97.4% of operable capacity means the answer cannot come from running the existing units harder.
capture_inputs.logistics_or_qualification: Product specification is the qualification: a barrel that is not on-spec ultra-low-sulfur cannot clear into the markets that lost the Russian cargo, whatever the crack is.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: The refiner. The record $102.20 crack and the above $60 European margin are the two cited prints, and both sit at this stage rather than at any input stage.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: RELIANCE.NS also appears on refinery-capacity-response, where it is the supply response rather than the incumbent. Holding it for both is one position, not two.

links.name: New conversion capacity outside Russia
links.role: The counter-response: Nigerian, Middle Eastern and Indian expansions add complex refining capacity that eventually closes the distillate gap, which makes this the link that ends the trade rather than one that rides it.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-006 shape: the world's reaction to the occurrence, wired in as its own link rather than left as narrative. The purest expressions (Dangote, Duqm, Yulong) are private or state-owned, so the listed proxies are partial.

capture_inputs.substitutability: This link IS the substitution. Its success is the invalidation of conversion-capacity and clean-product-shipping, which is why it belongs on the map rather than in a footnote.

links.name: Clean product tankers, LR2 and MR
links.role: The rerouted barrel has to float: Baltic short-haul MR voyages are replaced by Persian Gulf and India long hauls on LR2s, and the fleet is paid in ton-miles rather than in cargoes.

evidence.claim: The Platts LR2 index, for vessels without scrubbers and not eco-designed, rose from $57,204 per day at the beginning of June to $97,872 per day on July 14, with LR2s specifically commanding high premiums because of their better economics on long-distance journeys, while shadow fleet tankers are probably forced to wait for Russian loadings to recover rather than pursuing other uses.

source_excerpt: The Platts LR2 index, for vessels without scrubbers and not eco-designed, rose from $57,204 per day at the beginning of June to $97,872 per day on July 14.
LR2s, specifically, are commanding high premiums because of their better economics on long-distance journeys.
Shadow fleet tankers encounter specific difficulties and are probably forced to wait for Russian loadings to recover rather than pursuing other uses.

evidence.claim: MR earnings have averaged above $30,000 per day through much of 2024-2026, with peaks into the $40,000+ range, LR2 earnings cleared $50,000 per day consistently through 2024-2025, and the listed operators carrying this trade are Scorpio Tankers, Hafnia, Ardmore, TEN and Torm.

bottleneck.note: Ton-mile inflation with a supply response locked behind yard slots. The named risk is on the record and is not a modelling assumption: the shadow-fleet vessels displaced from the old short-haul trade are waiting, not exiting.

capture_inputs.substitutability: Dirty and clean fleets are different vessels with different owners, so crude-tanker capacity does not relieve this link. That separation is also why this map must not be merged with the Hormuz crude chain.
capture_inputs.logistics_or_qualification: Route length is the whole product: the same cargo tonnage pays more because it travels further, which is a physical fact rather than a price agreement.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: The owner, on the cited index prints. Whether it stayed in the P&L is a heat-stage question and no issuer figure is cited here.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: Latent supply is the honest hazard: shadow-fleet tonnage idled from the Baltic trade is not scrapped and has no public register, so the fleet is larger than the listed fleet.

links.name: Independent storage and blending terminals
links.role: Imported cargoes land in independent tank terminals at hubs like ARA, where gas oil is blended up to the local specification before it is sold, so this is where a long-haul barrel becomes a saleable one.

evidence.claim: At the terminal, gasoline, gas oil and diesel products can be stored and blended with other components bringing them up to specifications for the various international markets, and Royal Vopak is the world's largest independent tank storage service provider, specializing in the storage and handling of bulk liquid chemicals, gases and oil products.

Royal Vopak is the world's largest independent tank storage service provider, specializing in the storage and handling of bulk liquid chemicals, gases and oil products.

evidence.claim: US wholesale fuel distribution businesses are categorised by the terminals they run, from single-terminal regional operators to multi-terminal regional platforms, so terminal access is the physical input the distribution stage buys.

bottleneck.note: Hub tankage is scarce and permitted, but the largest operators in the cited hub (Oiltanking, VTTI, Koole) are private or trader-owned, so the listed expression is partial.

notes.text: The thesis was TESTED, not assumed, and it survives with one correction. The signal claims three separable links hide inside one headline: ULSD-capable hydrocracking, the LR2 product tankers, and the catalyst and turnaround suppliers. All three are here and all three cite separately. The correction is that the third is not one link but three that behave differently: hydroprocessing-catalysts (qualified per unit, concentrated, half of it private), refinery-hydrogen (a local monopoly at each refinery gate created by logistics, which no coverage of this occurrence mentions at all), and turnaround-and-catalyst-services (competitively bid labour with an ARCH-002 capture ceiling). Collapsing them would have put a HIGH-criticality gate and a MEDIUM-criticality contractor under one score.

Archetypes applied: ARCH-001 three times (hydroprocessing-technology on heavy-wall fabrication, shipyard-newbuild-capacity on dock slots, and conversion-capacity, which states the archetype's tell in its own role sentence); ARCH-002 twice (turnaround-and-catalyst-services, and wholesale-fuel-distribution, which is the same volume-without-capture trap wearing a distribution costume rather than an EPC one); ARCH-003 once, inverted (russian-refining-attrition sets every other link's demand and has no instrument); ARCH-004 twice (hydroprocessing-catalysts on substitutability, refinery-hydrogen on logistics, which is the cleanest logistics-leg instance in the corpus so far); ARCH-006 once (refinery-capacity-response). Absence checks, recorded because a missing archetype is a finding and not a gap to pad: ARCH-005 does NOT fire, there is no power-and-grid-equipment layer behind this story, and adding one to reach a familiar shape would have been invention; ARCH-007 does NOT fire, no semiconductor or compute layer sits anywhere on this chain, which is unusual across the corpus and is worth stating rather than passing over.

ARCH-006 note for the log. On tibet-mega-dam the counter-response link WAS the money corner. Here the counter-response is refinery-capacity-response, and it points the other way: the world's supply answer to this occurrence is the thing that ENDS the trade rather than the thing that rides it, and its purest expressions (Dangote, Duqm, Yulong) are private or state-owned. That is the second instance of the archetype and the first where it is a risk rather than an opportunity, which is a real amendment to the archetype's shape rather than a confirmation of it. Not auto-applied to _archetypes.md: escalated for Ron, since editing a HARDENED archetype's meaning is outside the repair lane.

Dedupe against SIG-20260829-04 (Hormuz), carried forward from the scanner's own note and acted on rather than restated. The two chains both lengthen tanker ton-miles, and merging them would invent an issuer census that does not exist: clean and dirty fleets are different vessels with different owners. clean-product-shipping here lists only clean-product owners (STNG, TRMD, HAFN, ASC, INSW, DIS.MI, 9104.T) and states the separation in its capture_inputs, so a later universe run cannot silently pool them.

Two stages I looked for and could NOT cite, recorded rather than invented. (a) A diesel additive and cold-flow / cetane blendstock link (Innospec, Infineum, Lubrizol, Evonik): plainly real, but no dated source opened this run that ties additive supply to this occurrence, and an uncited link is not a link. (b) A distillate strategic-reserve and emergency-stock release link (IEA collective action, EU 90-day obligations): the policy exists, but nothing dated and fetchable connected it to this ban, so it is named here instead of built. Both would have taken the map to 15 links; an honest 13 beats a padded 15.
